title: Electronic Voting Machine
summary: An 8051 academic hardware prototype for candidate input, vote counting and LCD result display, including debouncing and winner/tie logic.
overview: The Electronic Voting Machine is an academic embedded-system prototype using an 8051 microcontroller. Push buttons accept votes for multiple candidates, and a 16×2 LCD presents counts and calculated results. Embedded C logic handles switch debouncing, vote counting and winner or tie detection. Hardware photographs and a Proteus schematic document the implementation.
approach: Connected multiple-candidate push-button inputs to the 8051 control system.
Used software debouncing to handle mechanical switch inputs.
Implemented vote counts, result calculation and winner/tie logic in Embedded C.
Presented results through the LCD and assembled the photographed breadboard prototype.
outcomes: Implemented the academic voting-machine prototype shown in the hardware photographs.
Practised input handling, state/count logic and display interfacing in an embedded system.
The work is an educational prototype, without certification for use in real elections.
